clue.text: Inferior cow girl catches cold

indicators.note: the cow and girl placed together take hold of the cold letter between them

parts.note: a cow is something that lows, a lower
a lass is a girl
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A snobbish remark about a low-status milkmaid who has picked up a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' is a noun made from the verb 'low' (to moo): one who lows. 'catches' has the cow and girl together hold the cold letter between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower-class means of a lower social rank, hence inferior in the old snobbish sense.

clue.text: This girl is hugged by sailor, naturally

indicators.note: the name sits held inside the words that follow, wrapped by their letters

explanation.surface: A girl naturally gets an embrace from a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The name spans the end of 'sailor' and the start of 'naturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorna is a girl's name, as in the novel Lorna Doone.

clue.text: Chaps who should know what's in store

definitions.text: Chaps who should know what's in store

parts.words: Chaps who should know what's in store
parts.note: people who know the future, read literally as staff who know the contents of a storage building

explanation.surface: Men who ought to be able to predict the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in store' suggests the future; read literally it means the stock kept in a store.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers in a storage depot keep track of the goods held there.

clue.text: King with honour producing garment

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king (Rex)
the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A monarch bestowing an award produces ceremonial clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose garment.

clue.text: All the changes of a deadly nature

indicators.note: the letters of the two words go through changes, rearranging into new order

explanation.surface: All the alterations are fatal ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethal describes something able to kill, so deadly in nature.

clue.text: Hidden under lots of loose rocks is Edmund

indicators.note: in a down answer, the name for Edmund comes below the rocks

parts.note: scree is a mass of loose stones on a slope
Ned is a short form of Edmund

explanation.surface: Edmund lies concealed beneath a heap of rubble.
explanation.definitionFit: Screened means shielded from view, so concealed.

clue.text: Bakery — I'd chat about one of its products maybe

indicators.note: the letters are moved about, rearranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A baker's shop gossiping about what it makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to the bakery, so the definition leans on the fodder word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cake for an anniversary of someone's birth is a typical item a bakery sells.

clue.text: Model and artist turned up to make a bit of money

parts.note: a doll is a small model of a person

indicators.note: in a down answer the artist's letters go upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A fashion model and a painter arrived to earn some cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollar is a unit of currency, a single piece of cash.

clue.text: Valuable coin found in item of food

parts.note: something rare is scarce and so valuable
a bit is an old name for a small coin, as in threepenny bit

explanation.surface: A prized coin turns up inside a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit, Welsh rabbit, is melted cheese on toast, a snack dish.

clue.text: Animal fancied occupying the back of your house

indicators.note: only the rear letter of the word your is taken
the popular word fills the inside of the house abbreviation

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular, so fancied

explanation.surface: A beast someone imagined is living at the rear of your home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancied' is not an anagram signal here: it means popular, 'in', and 'occupying' puts it inside the house abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is a large thick-skinned horned animal.

clue.text: One going round hospital in pain

indicators.note: the word for one surrounds the hospital letter

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone touring a hospital while hurting.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous hurt.

clue.text: Dad has system of paying — such is his family duty

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a rental is an arrangement of paying for use of something

explanation.surface: A father on a payment plan sees it as his responsibility to the family.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the kind of duty a dad has: one owed by a mother or father.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty a father or mother owes their children is described as a parental one.

clue.text: Margaret, a very good type, a right "superperson"

parts.note: Meg is a pet form of Margaret
ST, saint, is a very good person

explanation.surface: Margaret, a saintly sort, is a real superwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a very good type' splits as A + ST, and 'a right' as A + R.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastar is a hugely famous celebrity, someone beyond an ordinary star.

clue.text: Manage to secure superior type of vehicle

indicators.note: the word for manage holds the letter for superior fast inside it

parts.note: to cope is to manage
U stands for upper class, superior

explanation.surface: Contriving to obtain a classier sort of car.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupé is a two-door car with a fixed roof.

clue.text: Sings about Hampshire

parts.note: C, circa, means about
Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county on the south coast

explanation.surface: A singer whose songs are about an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Chants means sings in a monotone or intones.

clue.text: Fellow ejected from chapel, the German high-up in congregation

indicators.note: the fellow is thrown out of the word chapel, leaving what remains

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A man thrown out of chapel, the German being a senior church figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a senior lay officer in some churches, such as Presbyterian ones.

clue.text: Commotion in place of rest left in the morning

parts.note: a bed is where one rests
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: An uproar in the bedroom after someone left early.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam is a scene of uproar and confusion, from the old London asylum.

clue.text: Declare times in statistical information

parts.note: to aver is to declare or assert
ages are long periods, times

explanation.surface: Announcing timings within a set of figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Means and medians are figures summarising data, a kind of statistics.

clue.text: Crew said something at Chiswick in boat race

definitions.text: something at Chiswick in boat race

indicators.note: the crew word is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A rowing crew comments on the Boat Race passing Chiswick.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing race on the Thames, which passes Chiswick Eyot, a small river island in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot (ait) is a small island in a river, and one lies on the race course at Chiswick.

clue.text: Rows with ferocious beasts, not good

indicators.note: the beasts are without the good letter

parts.note: tigers are fierce big cats

explanation.surface: Arguments involving savage animals that behave badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiers are rows or levels placed one above another, as of seats.

clue.text: Some frantic person opposing something

indicators.note: only some of the letters of frantic are taken, a run from inside it

explanation.surface: A rather frenzied protester.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is someone against a policy or idea, an opponent.

clue.text: Taking newspaper

definitions.meaning: the act of stealing, taking what belongs to another
read as two words, the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is taking property unlawfully; the Financial Times is abbreviated FT.

clue.text: Fantastic eagle in descent

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or wildly strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A marvellous bird of prey swooping downward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'descent' looks like the eagle's dive but means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is one's line of ancestry, the family one comes from.

clue.text: Sour disposition of US men, prigs being awkward

indicators.note: awkward letters are out of order, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: American men and prigs being difficult, showing a bad temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumpiness is bad-tempered sulkiness, an ill-humoured mood.
